items.label: text
items.text: The oil industry is at the very heart of modern life. It provides fuels, plastics and the organic chemicals which go to make things as different as solvents, drugs, dyes and explosives. This chapter explores how an unappealing, sticky, black liquid is converted into useful things.

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 23.1 The oil industry is BIG business!

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know that crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe how the industrial process of fractional distillation separates crude oil into fractions

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know the names and uses of the main fractions obtained from crude oil: refinery gases, gasoline, kerosene, diesel, fuel oil and bitumen

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know the trend in colour, boiling point and viscosity of the main fractions

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know that a fuel is a substance that, when burned, releases heat energy

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know the possible products of complete and incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons with oxygen in the air

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know that in car engines the temperature reached is high enough to allow nitrogen and oxygen from air to react, forming oxides of nitrogen

items.label: list_item
items.text: Explain how the combustion of some impurities in hydrocarbon fuels results in the formation of sulfur dioxide

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand how sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen contribute to acid rain

items.label: list_item
items.text: Describe how long-chain alkanes are converted to alkenes and shorter-chain alkanes by catalytic cracking (using silica or alumina as the catalyst and a temperature in the range of 600–700 °C)

items.label: list_item
items.text: Explain why cracking is necessary in terms of the balance between supply and demand for different fractions
